taglines: It's Saturday. The weekend you promised yourself would be 'intentional and restorative' has already devolved into a browser tab situation that cannot be explained to anyone who wasn't there.
Someone on the internet is wrong about something and you found out about it at 8:43 AM before coffee and now the whole day has a different texture to it. This is called having passions.
You opened your laptop 'just to check one thing.' That was ninety minutes ago. The one thing has spawned six more things. The original thing has not been checked. It never will be.

The plan was to go outside today. You are not outside. You are in the same chair as yesterday in a slightly different posture. Progress is nonlinear and that's what the productivity gurus keep saying so.

Saturday morning brain is a fascinating phenomenon: completely incapable of responding to emails but fully available to restructure the entire mental model of a project that doesn't need restructuring.

Your phone has forty-two unread notifications. You are aware of this. You are choosing to leave them unread in the same way someone chooses to leave a structural crack in a wall by simply not owning a flashlight.
Brunch is a scam designed to make you spend fourteen dollars on eggs while sitting too close to strangers who are also trying to have a quiet morning. You are having eggs at home. You are winning.

A thing you're building might actually work and you know this because you caught yourself explaining it out loud to no one in an empty room at 9 AM on a Saturday. That's the tell. That's always the tell.
